Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: BUG-004, report failed Telegram tracking-comment writes

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8895` @ `b79b58cf49a9555c4152d764efa6aaec782fc2d9` (integration branch metadata matches; mismatch=false). Refs #8895, which is the tracking issue. This plan is for the orchestrator-managed child issue `bug004-tg-tracking-write-status`.

### Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- Changes existing code only. No new script, supervisor or DB work. Nothing needs a `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.
- Entry point: no new trigger. The helpers already run inside every workflow that sources `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`. The new test runs on PR push through the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` step "Tracking issue comment cap tests" (line 1109).

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`
- `tests/test_tg_tracking_write_status.py` (new)
- `tests/test_tracking_comment_cap.py`
- `agents.d/wfopt-2026-10-03-2-tg-tracking-write.md` (new)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Functions or modules to implement

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _tg_delete_msg_checked
Scope-mode justification: The issue sets the exact contract: which writes change, the warning format, the retry policy, best-effort semantics and what must not change. The plan delivers exactly that. It reuses the status-capture pattern already in `_tg_delete_msg_checked` (`scripts/tg_helpers.sh` around lines 206-240: `curl -s --max-time N -w '%{http_code}'`, then check the 3-digit code). It does not invent a new mechanism. There are six writes, not four. Besides the four the issue names, each helper has a second create POST that runs when the comments fetch fails. Those POSTs have the same defect, and the shared helper covers them for about 6 extra lines. Under the Boil the Lake rule (well under 30 LOC, no new dependency or interface) and §6 (Correctness & safety ranks above Speed), they go through the same helper. See D3.

1. **New private helper `_tg_tracking_write`** in `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`, placed just above `tg_store_msg_id` (around line 450). The name is confirmed unused in `scripts/`, `tests/` and `agents.md`.
   - Signature: `_tg_tracking_write <op> <issue_num> <phase> <msg_id> <method> <url> <json_body>`
     - `op` is `append` or `create`.
     - `phase` is the phase name, or the literal `none` for `tg_store_msg_id`.
     - `method` is `PATCH` or `POST`.
   - Body, tab-indented, braces on a new line, every variable `local`:
     - Set `IFS=$' \t\n'` locally, as `_tg_delete_msg_checked` does.
     - `max_attempts=1`. Set it to `2` only when `op=append` and `method=PATCH`.
     - Loop `attempt=1..max_attempts`:
       - Run `http_code=$(curl -s --max-time 30 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X "${method}" -H "Authorization: token ${GH_TOKEN}" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" "${url}" -d "${json_body}" 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?`, resetting `rc=0` before each attempt.
       - If `rc==0` and `http_code` matches `^2[0-9][0-9]$`, return 0.
       - If `http_code` is not exactly 3 digits, set it to `000`.
       - If `attempt < max_attempts`, run `sleep 2` and continue.
     - After the last attempt: `echo "::warning::TG_TRACKING_WRITE_FAILED issue=${issue_num} op=${op} phase=${phase} msg_id=${msg_id} http=${http_code}" >&2`, then `return 0`.
   - The helper must never print to stdout. `-o /dev/null` discards the response body, and the `-w` output goes into a variable. It must never log the URL, the token or a body.
   - Callers run under `set -euo pipefail`, so every command whose failure is tolerated uses `|| rc=$?`. The helper always returns 0.
2. **`tg_store_msg_id`**: replace the three raw `curl ... >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` writes. Every other line stays unchanged.
   - Fetch-failure fallback (around line 474): `_tg_tracking_write create "${issue_num}" none "${msg_id}" POST "${api_base}/${issue_num}/comments" "$(jq -n --arg b "<!-- tg_cleanup:${msg_id} -->" '{body: $b}')"`. Keep the existing `::warning::Failed to fetch…` line before it and the `return 0` after it.
   - Append (around line 502): `_tg_tracking_write append "${issue_num}" none "${msg_id}" PATCH "https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/comments/${tracking_id}" "$(jq -n --arg b "${new_body}" '{body: $b}')"`.
   - Create (around line 509): same as the fallback.
3. **`tg_store_phase_msg_id`**: the same three replacements (around lines 554, 582 and 588), with `"${phase}"` instead of `none` and the existing `tg_phase:${phase}:` bodies.
4. Do not touch `_tg_newest_comments_json`, `_tg_tracking_author_login`, the trusted-author jq selection, the `sed` marker rewrite, the marker formats, `_tg_valid_phase` or any cleanup function.

## Data structures affected
- None. The comment bodies `<!-- tg_cleanup:… -->` and `<!-- tg_phase:<phase>:… -->` stay byte-identical.
- New log line on stderr: `::warning::TG_TRACKING_WRITE_FAILED issue=<n> op=<append|create> phase=<phase|none> msg_id=<id> http=<3-digit code|000>`

## API or interface changes
- No public function signature changes. `tg_store_msg_id` and `tg_store_phase_msg_id` take the same arguments and still always return 0.
- New contractual log prefix `TG_TRACKING_WRITE_FAILED`, registered in `agents.d/wfopt-2026-10-03-2-tg-tracking-write.md`:
  - The block starts with `<!-- agents: section="Stable log prefixes (contractual)" -->`.
  - Then a `` - `TG_TRACKING_WRITE_FAILED` `` bullet that names `scripts/tg_helpers.sh` and `_tg_tracking_write`. It gives the field format, states that `http=000` means a curl transport failure or timeout, that PATCH (append) is retried once after 2s, that POST (create) is never retried, that the line is diagnostics only, that the helper still returns 0, and that the token and bodies are never logged.
  - Then `LOG_PREFIX.name=TG_TRACKING_WRITE_FAILED`.
  - `agents.md` is not edited (§25).
- GitHub API volume (§14): no new calls on the success path. On a failed append, at most one extra PATCH.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` line 1109: append `tests/test_tg_tracking_write_status.py` to the existing pytest command in the "Tracking issue comment cap tests" step. `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` requires this. The file is 171,639 bytes, so §24 headroom is fine. 2-space YAML indent.

## Decisions

### D1 — One shared private helper instead of six inline curl blocks
- **Chosen:** `_tg_tracking_write` holds the status capture, the retry policy and the warning. All six call sites call it.
- **Alternatives considered:** duplicate the `-w` / status check / warning inline at each site.
- **Why:** Six copies of retry logic drift apart. One helper keeps the PATCH-only retry rule in one tested place, and the diff stays smaller.

### D2 — Retry PATCH once after a fixed 2-second sleep; never retry POST
- **Chosen:** `max_attempts=2` only for `op=append`/PATCH, with `sleep 2` hard-coded. No new env var.
- **Alternatives considered:** a configurable sleep env var; retrying POST with dedup by re-reading the comments.
- **Why:** The issue requires a single retry for the idempotent PATCH (the full body is sent again) and no blind POST retry, because a timed-out POST may already have created the comment. A fixed value adds no env surface (§8). Tests avoid the real wait by defining a `sleep` shell function after sourcing, which takes precedence over the external command.

### D3 — Also cover the two fetch-failure fallback create POSTs
- **Chosen:** Route the fallback POSTs in both helpers through `_tg_tracking_write create …`.
- **Alternatives considered:** change only the four writes the issue names and leave the fallbacks silent.
- **Why:** These are also "create POST in `tg_store_msg_id` / `tg_store_phase_msg_id`" and have the same silent-loss defect. The cost is a few lines through the same helper. They report as `op=create`, which fits the required format.

### D4 — Keep raw `curl` instead of `curl_gh_api`
- **Chosen:** Call `curl` directly with `-s --max-time 30 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'`.
- **Alternatives considered:** use `curl_gh_api`, the rate-limit wrapper from `gh_helpers.sh`.
- **Why:** The issue specifies curl with `-w`/`-o`/`--max-time`. A wrapper with its own retry policy could re-send the non-idempotent POST, which the issue forbids. 30 s matches the other GitHub calls in this file (`--max-time 30`).

### D5 — Report transport failures as `http=000`
- **Chosen:** Any non-zero curl exit, or a code that is not 3 digits, is reported as `http=000`.
- **Alternatives considered:** add a `curl_rc=` field.
- **Why:** The issue fixes the warning field set. curl itself writes `000` for `%{http_code}` when no response arrived.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary:** GitHub REST API responses are untrusted. Only the 3-digit status is read, and the body goes to `/dev/null`, so no response content reaches the logs.
- **Secrets:** the `GH_TOKEN` header is never echoed. curl stderr goes to `/dev/null`. The warning contains only the issue number, op, a validated phase (`_tg_valid_phase` already rejects anything else), the numeric message ID and the code.
- **Authorization:** unchanged. The trusted-author selection (#8598) still decides which comment ID is PATCHed. The retry re-sends the same PATCH to the same, already-vetted ID.
- **Abuse cases:**
  - A forged look-alike marker still only leads to a new POST. Existing tests cover this and still pass.
  - A hostile or failing API cannot make the helper loop: at most 2 PATCH attempts, each bounded by 30 s.
  - A hostile API cannot fail the caller, because the helper always returns 0.
- No money handling is involved.

Data flow:
1. `tg_send_tracked` / `tg_send_phase_tracked` → `tg_store_*`.
2. `_tg_newest_comments_json` → trusted-author marker lookup.
3. `_tg_tracking_write` runs one of:
   - append: PATCH; on non-2xx or a curl error, sleep 2 and PATCH again; if that also fails, emit the warning.
   - create: POST; on non-2xx or a curl error, emit the warning, with no retry.
4. Retu
